newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa rejects cartel body criticism [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT].
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa rejects cartel body criticism [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT].

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Wednesday rejected criticism from the Federal Cartel Office that fares on its Frankfurt-Berlin route were too high and queried the legal standing of the office's warning to it.

"The warning itself has no legal effect of its own and comprises a number of legally disputed questions," the airline said in a statement. It added it would seek a full legal clarification of the implications as soon as possible.
A Lufthansa spokesman said in response to enquiries the airline would in the meantime officially reject the warning.

Lufthansa, which charges 840 marks for its return Frankfurt-Berlin Business Class fare, said such a fare could not represent an abuse of its dominant market position because it failed to cover its costs on the route.
"Companies cannot be forced to set prices, which make break-even or profit-yielding production possible," it said.
It added: "The fact that another competitor has for years flown along its domestic German routes at a loss underlines that the routes cannot be served in a commercially viable way".
(Corrects by deleting incorrect statement that Deutsche BA flies the Frankfurt to Berlin route).
